title.narrative: Sustainable Assistance for Inclusion and Livelihoods (SAIL) Project for Manta Community

description.narrative:
The Manta community, a floating fishing group in Bangladesh's Barishal region, faces severe displacement and vulnerability due to climate change. Around 10,000 Manta people live on boats, with approximately 5,000 children out of school. The community remains largely deprived of education and basic government facilities, with most members lacking literacy and essential life skills. Women particularly struggle with basic numeracy, making them vulnerable in trade [The Daily Star, February-2023]. Living on boats exposes them to harsh weather conditions, including storms, cyclones, and intense sun exposure. Their mobile lifestyle and lack of national identity cards create barriers to accessing education, healthcare, and government aid. The community also faces legal challenges and cultural exclusion. Their traditional fishing livelihood has become increasingly unsustainable due to overfishing, competition from commercial fishers, and extreme weather events, forcing many to venture into deeper waters and incur rising debt [ICCCAD, December-2023]. The Sustainable Assistance for Inclusion and Livelihoods (SAIL) Project, implemented by the Association of Voluntary Actions for Society (AVAS), aims to address these challenges. Running from March 1 to September 30, 2025, with a budget of 30,000 GBP (4,477,612 BDT), the project will support approximately 200 households (1,000 individuals) in Barishal division, allocating BDT 22,338 per household on average. SAIL project will specifically focus on: · Livelihood support through training, financial assistance, and alternative income-generating activities
· Informal education for the elderly groups and children to increase literacy rates, basic counting skills, signature and so on.
· Healthcare access through medical camps and hygiene awareness session.
· Protection, WaSH, referral, basic climate change knowledge through courtyard sessions.
· Social inclusion and advocacy to improve recognition and rights of the Manta people.
